abbasid: Black was the Abbasids' colour from their revolt in 747.
achaemenid: Xenophon wrote that the Persian kings marched under a golden eagle with spread wings, raised on a spear.
af-1901: Black with the white seal of the emir.
af-1930: Flag of the Kingdom of Afghanistan
Black, red and green with the mosque, 1928-1973.
af-1980: Flag of the Democratic Republic of Afghanistan
Black, red and green with the state emblem, 1980-1992.
af-1992: Flag of the Islamic State of Afghanistan
af-black: Abdur Rahman Khan's plain black flag, 1880-1901.
af-taliban: The Taliban's white flag with the Shahada, 1997-2001 and again from 2021.
al-1946: The eagle with a red star, 1946-1992.
almohad: The Almohads marched under white standards.
arab-fed: Flag of the Federation of Arab Republics
The Hawk of Quraish, flown by Egypt, Syria and Libya in the 1970s.
aragon: Four red bars on gold, the arms of the counts of Barcelona and kings of Aragon.
asturias: The jewelled Cross of Victory, given by Alfonso III in 908, emblem of the first Christian kingdom of Spain.
austria-hungary: The civil ensign of 1869: Austria's red-white-red beside Hungary's red-white-green.
ba-1992: White with the lilies of Kotromanić.
ba-kotromanic: Banner of the Kingdom of Bosnia
The Kotromanić arms: lilies on blue, crossed by a white bend.
bavaria: The white and blue lozenges of the Wittelsbach dukes and kings of Bavaria.
bf-volta: Black, white and red, the Volta rivers, 1959-1984.
bg-1971: Flag of the People's Republic of Bulgaria
bj-1975: Flag of the People's Republic of Benin
br-empire: Flag of the Empire of Brazil
Green and gold with the imperial arms, 1822-1889.
brittany: Plain ermine, the arms of the dukes of Brittany from 1316.
burgundy-cross: The ragged red saltire of Burgundy, carried by Spain's armies and ships from 1506 to 1785.
byz-tetra: A gold cross between four firesteels (often read as Bs), flown by the empire from the 1260s until 1453.
ca-red: Canada's flag in practice from 1868 to 1965, when the maple leaf replaced it.
carthage: The sign of the goddess Tanit, carved on thousands of Carthaginian stones. No Carthaginian flag survives.
castile: A gold castle on red, the arms of the kings of Castile.
castile-leon: Banner of the Crown of Castile
The castles of Castile quartered with the lions of León, after the crowns joined in 1230.
cathay: How the Catalan Atlas of 1375 drew the flag of the Great Khan in China: three red crescents.
cd-1877: Flag of the Congo Free State
Blue with a gold star: Leopold II's Congo Free State and then the Belgian Congo, until 1960.
cd-1960: Flag of the Republic of the Congo
cd-1963: Flag of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, 1963-1971
central-america: Flag of the Federal Republic of Central America
Blue, white and blue, still the colours of its five republics, 1823-1841.
cg-1970: Flag of the People's Republic of the Congo
cy-lusignan: Banner of the Kingdom of Cyprus
Jerusalem, Lusignan, Cyprus and Armenia quartered, the arms of the Lusignan kings, 1192-1489.
ddr: The German Democratic Republic, with the hammer and compass, 1959-1990.
de-empire: Black, white and red, the North German Confederation and the German Empire, 1867-1918 (and co-official 1933-1935).
de-nazi: The flag of the Nazi dictatorship, 1935-1945.
delhi: Black flag of the Delhi Sultanate
The Catalan Atlas of 1375 shows Delhi's coastal cities under a black flag, the colour of the Abbasid caliphs the sultans recognised.
eg-1867: Flag of the Khedivate of Egypt
Egypt under the Muhammad Ali dynasty, 1867-1922.
eg-1922: Flag of the Kingdom of Egypt
eg-1953: Red, white and black with the eagle, 1953-1958.
eic-1707: Flag of the East India Company
Thirteen red and white stripes with the Union in the corner, 1707-1801.
eic-1801: Flag of the East India Company
The Company's flag after the Union of 1801, until its rule ended in 1858.
en-royal: Three gold lions on red, the arms of the English kings from Richard I.
es-1785: Red and gold, chosen by Charles III in 1785 for his navy.
es-1931: Flag of the Second Spanish Republic
es-franco: The red and gold with the eagle of Saint John, 1938-1981.
et-1897: Green, gold and red with the Lion of Judah, from Menelik II to 1974.
et-1987: Flag of the People's Democratic Republic of Ethiopia
fatimid: The Fatimids took white as their dynastic colour; their caliphal banners were also red and yellow.
fr-ancien: Gold lilies strewn on blue, the arms of the Capetian kings ("France Ancient").
fr-bourbon: White flag of the Bourbon Restoration
The returning Bourbon kings flew white, 1814-1830.
fr-moderne: Three gold lilies on blue, the kings' arms from Charles V (c. 1376) to the Revolution.
gb-1707: England's cross over Scotland's saltire, 1606 at sea and 1707-1801 for the kingdom.
ge-1918: Flag of the Democratic Republic of Georgia
geneva: Half the imperial eagle and the key of Saint Peter.
genoa: Flag of the Republic of Genoa
Saint George's red cross on white.
gr-cross: Flag of the Kingdom of Greece
The white cross on blue, Greece's land flag, 1822-1969.
gran-colombia: Francisco de Miranda's yellow, blue and red, flown by Bolívar's republic, 1821-1831.
habsburg: Black and gold flag of Austria
The Habsburg colours, flag of the Austrian Empire.
han: Red was the colour of the Han, ruling by the element fire.
hanover: The white Saxon steed on red.
hawaii: Flag of the Kingdom of Hawaii
Eight stripes for the eight islands, with the Union Flag, 1845-1893.
hbc: Flag of the Hudson's Bay Company
The company that ruled Rupert's Land until 1870.
hejaz: Flag of the Kingdom of Hejaz
The flag of the Arab Revolt, 1916, kept by the Hashemite kingdom in the Hejaz until 1925.
horde: As drawn on the Catalan Atlas of 1375: the tamga, the khans' mark, also stamped on their coins.
hr-checky: The red and white checkerboard, Croatia's arms from the 1400s.
hre-1: Banner of the Holy Roman Empire
The black imperial eagle on gold, the emperors' banner from the 1100s.
hre-2: Banner of the Holy Roman Empire
The double-headed eagle, used by the emperors from Sigismund (1433) until the empire ended in 1806.
ht-1806: Blue over red, from 1806 (the arms were added later).
hu-arms: Banner of the Kingdom of Hungary
The Árpád stripes beside the double cross on its green hill.
hu-arpad: Red and white stripes, the arms of the Árpád kings.
ie-harp: Flag of the Kingdom of Ireland
in-raj: The red ensign with the Star of India, flown for British India from 1880 to 1947.
iq-1921: Flag of the Kingdom of Iraq
ir-1907: Iran's green, white and red flag with the lion and the sun, 1907-1979.
iso:ar: Sky blue and white with the Sun of May, from 1812.
iso:at: Red, white and red, by legend the bloodied tunic of Duke Leopold V at Acre in 1191.
iso:cd: Flag of Congo, The Democratic Republic of the
iso:ch: The white cross of Schwyz, carried by the Swiss confederates since the 1300s.
iso:cn: The People's Republic of China, since 1949.
iso:de: The colours of the 1848 revolution: the Weimar Republic from 1919, West Germany from 1949, all Germany since 1990.
iso:dk: By legend it fell from the sky during a Danish battle in Estonia in 1219: the oldest national flag still in use.
iso:eg: Red, white and black with the Eagle of Saladin, since 1984.
iso:fr: Blue, white and red, the colours of the Revolution, the national flag from 1794.
iso:gb: The crosses of England, Scotland and Ireland together, since 1801.
iso:gb-eng: The red cross of Saint George, England's flag from the late 1200s.
iso:gb-sct: By legend a white saltire appeared in the sky before a Scottish victory in 832.
iso:ge: The red crosses on white of medieval Georgia, made the national flag again in 2004.
iso:hu: Red, white and green, first raised in the revolution of 1848.
iso:in: Saffron, white and green with the Ashoka wheel, since 1947.
iso:iq: Red, white and black with "God is great", since 2008.
iso:ir: Green, white and red with the emblem of the Islamic Republic, since 1980.
iso:it: Green, white and red, first raised in 1797; without the royal arms since 1946.
iso:jp: The red sun. Emperor Monmu raised a sun banner at court in 701; Japan's national flag from 1870.
iso:kn: Flag of Saint Kitts and Nevis
iso:kr: Korea's flag from 1883; South Korea's since 1948.
iso:lk: The lion of the old Sinhalese kings, with stripes added for Sri Lanka's minorities.
iso:ma: The old red flag with the green star of Solomon added in 1915.
iso:mx: The eagle on a cactus, from the founding legend of Tenochtitlan.
iso:nl: Red, white and blue, which replaced the orange of the Prince's Flag in the 1600s.
iso:np: Two stacked pennants, the only national flag that is not a rectangle.
iso:om: The old red flag with white and green added in 1970.
iso:pl: White over red, the colours of the white eagle on red.
iso:ru: White, blue and red, first flown on Peter the Great's ships in the 1690s.
iso:se: The gold cross on blue, flown since the 1500s.
iso:th: Red, white and blue, which replaced the white elephant in 1917.
iso:tn: Red with a crescent and star, from 1831.
iso:tr: The Ottoman flag from 1844, and Turkey's since.
iso:tw: Blue Sky, White Sun, Red Earth
The flag of the Republic of China from 1928; on Taiwan since 1949.
iso:vc: Flag of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines
it-savoy: Flag of the Kingdom of Italy
The tricolour with the arms of Savoy, 1848-1946.
kalmar: A red cross on gold, the union of Denmark, Norway and Sweden, 1397-1523.
kandy: Flag of the Kingdom of Kandy
The lion flag of the last Sinhalese kingdom, taken by the British in 1815.
kh-1976: Red with Angkor Wat in yellow, 1975-1989.
la-1952: Flag of the Kingdom of Laos
Erawan, the three-headed white elephant under a parasol, 1952-1975.
labarum: The Chi-Rho standard Constantine took into battle in 312; Christian emperors kept it as their banner.
leon: A purple lion on white, the arms of the kings of León.
lt-vytis: The white knight on a red field, the arms of the grand dukes of Lithuania.
ly-1951: Flag of the Kingdom of Libya
ly-1969: Flag of the Libyan Arab Republic
ma-red: The plain red flag of the Alaouite sultans; the green star was added in 1915.
mamluk: Mamluk sultans flew yellow banners (sometimes red); the Catalan Atlas of 1375 draws a crescent on Cairo's.
manchukuo: The Japanese puppet state in Manchuria, 1932-1945.
maratha: The saffron swallow-tailed banner of Shivaji and the Maratha Confederacy.
me-krstas: The red battle flag of Montenegro with its white cross.
mm-1948: Flag of the Union of Burma
mm-1974: Flag of the Socialist Republic of the Union of Burma
mn-1945: Flag of the Mongolian People's Republic
With the socialist star above the Soyombo, 1940-1992.
mongol: The Mongols flew no cloth flags. Chinggis Khan's standard was the Tug, a spear hung with white horsetails.
mongol-white: Like other Mongol and Turkic dynasties, the Ilkhans preferred white banners.
muscovy: The double-headed eagle Ivan III took up after marrying the Byzantine princess Sophia Palaiologina.
mx-1821: Flag of the First Mexican Empire
The crowned eagle of Agustín de Iturbide, 1821-1823.
my-1950: Flag of the Federation of Malaya
navarre: Gold chains on red, the arms of Navarre from about 1234.
nejd: Flag of the First Saudi State
Green with the Shahada, the flag of the Emirate of Diriyah and later of Nejd.
new-granada: Flag of the Republic of New Granada
no-1814: The Danish flag with the Norwegian lion, used after independence from Denmark.
no-lion: The gold lion with Saint Olaf's axe, from about 1280.
ofs: Flag of the Orange Free State
Orange and white stripes with the Dutch flag, 1857-1902.
oman-red: The plain red flag of the sultans of Muscat and Oman, used until 1970.
ottoman-red: Ottoman armies and ships flew red and green flags with crescents; the star was added in 1844.
papal: Yellow and white with the keys and the papal tiara, 1803-1870.
papal-old: The crossed keys of Saint Peter.
pe-bo-confederation: Red, with the arms of its three states, 1836-1839.
pl-eagle: Banner of the Kingdom of Poland
The crowned white eagle on red, Poland's arms from 1295.
pl-lt: The white eagle of Poland quartered with the knight of Lithuania.
plc: Red and white with the arms of the Commonwealth, 1569-1795.
prinsenvlag: Orange, white and blue, the colours of William of Orange, flown in the Dutch Revolt.
prussia: The black eagle on white, Prussia's arms since the Teutonic Order.
pt-1830: Flag of the Kingdom of Portugal
Blue and white, the constitutional monarchy, 1830-1910.
pt-old: The arms of Portugal (five blue shields inside a red border of castles) on white.
qajar: Qajar Iran flew the lion and the sun on a white field, edged in green.
qin: Black was the colour of the Qin, ruling by the element water.
qing: Made the national flag in 1889; a triangular version flew from 1862. Before that the Qing had banners, not a flag.
roc-5: The Republic of China, 1912-1928: one stripe for each of the Han, Manchu, Mongol, Hui and Tibetan peoples.
rome-spqr: Rome had no national flag. Its legions marched under the eagle and the red vexillum, and SPQR stood for the Senate and People of Rome.
rs-1835: Flag of the Principality of Serbia
rs-nemanjic: The white double-headed eagle of medieval Serbia.
rus-trident: The trident sign of Prince Volodymyr the Great, struck on his coins. Rus had no flag.
safavid: Shah Abbas the Great set the lion and the sun on the green flag of Safavid Iran.
sasanian: The jewelled royal banner of the Sasanian kings, said to be the leather apron of the blacksmith Kaveh. It was lost at al-Qadisiyyah in 636.
savoy: The white cross of the dukes of Savoy, also flown by the Kingdom of Sardinia.
saxony: White and green, the Kingdom of Saxony.
se-1818: Sweden's flag with Norway's saltire in the corner, 1818-1844.
se-1844: With the union mark of Sweden and Norway, 1844-1905.
se-crowns: Three gold crowns on blue, the Swedish kings' arms from 1336.
siam-chakra: Flag of Siam with the chakra
Rama II added the white chakra of Vishnu, 1817.
siam-elephant: King Mongkut set a white elephant on the red flag in 1855; it flew until the stripes of 1917.
siam-red: Siam's plain red flag, flown from the late 1600s.
sicily-arag: Banner of the Kingdom of Sicily
The bars of Aragon and the eagles of the Hohenstaufen, the arms of the Aragonese kings of Sicily.
st-john: Flag of the Knights of Saint John
The white cross on red of the Knights Hospitaller.
su: The hammer and sickle with the red star, 1922-1991.
sv-1865: Blue and white stripes with red and stars.
sy-1932: Flown at independence, in 1932-1958 and 1961-1963, by the 2011 uprising, and as the national flag again from 2025.
teutonic: The black cross on white of the Teutonic Knights.
texas: Flag of the Republic of Texas
The Lone Star flag, adopted in 1839 and still the flag of Texas.
three-stars: The planned union of Egypt, Syria and Iraq, 1963: Syria flew it until 1972 and Iraq until 1991.
tibet: Flown by the government of the 13th Dalai Lama from 1916 until 1959.
timurid: Timur's mark, three rings, which the Castilian envoy Clavijo saw on his coins and seals in 1404.
transvaal: The four-colour flag of the South African Republic (Transvaal), 1858-1902.
trucial: Red with a white border, required of the Gulf sheikhdoms by their 1820 treaty with Britain.
uar: Flag of the United Arab Republic
The union of Egypt and Syria, 1958-1961; Egypt kept it until 1972, and Syria took it back in 1980.
umayyad: White was the Umayyads' dynastic colour.
united-tribes: Flag of the United Tribes of New Zealand
Chosen by Māori chiefs in 1834, and flown by many hapū after 1840.

venice: Flag of the Republic of Venice
The winged lion of Saint Mark on red.
vergina: The sixteen-rayed star of the Macedonian kings, found on the gold chest in the tomb of Philip II at Vergina.
ye-mutawakkil: Flag of the Kingdom of Yemen
The Mutawakkilite kingdom, 1918-1962: a sword and five stars.

Orange, white and blue with three small flags (Britain, the Orange Free State and Transvaal), 1928-1994.

zanzibar: The plain red flag of the Omani sultans of Zanzibar.
